## Hook (first 3 seconds)
**On-screen text (burned-in, muted-safe):** "Your ₹220 espresso has ₹31 of coffee in it."
**Visual:** A single espresso shot, overhead, with a price tag reading **₹220** resting beside the cup.
*Hook archetype: Specific Number. The figure is surprising and it IS the whole claim — no setup.*

## Body (3-4 scenes with cues)

**Scene 1 — the coffee (0:03–0:08)**
On-screen: "Beans: ₹31"
Visual: Ground coffee tipped into the portafilter; the ₹220 tag stays in-frame, now with ₹31 highlighted against it.
Caption/VO: "That's 18 grams of specialty beans, roasted this month. The best part of the cup — and the smallest line on the bill."

**Scene 2 — where the rest goes (0:08–0:14)**
On-screen: "Milk, cup, gas, power: ₹44"
Visual: Quick cuts — steam wand, takeaway cup, the meter ticking.
Caption/VO: "Add what surrounds it. Still under a fifth of the price."

**Scene 3 — the real cost (0:14–0:21)**
On-screen: "Rent + the person who made it: ₹112"
Visual: Wide shot of the café; barista pulling the shot, slowing down for the pour.
Caption/VO: "The biggest number isn't the coffee. It's the room you sit in and the hands that made it. That's who the ₹220 pays."

**Scene 4 — the payoff (0:21–0:26)**
On-screen: "₹31 coffee. ₹189 everything else."
Visual: The finished espresso back overhead, tag now fully broken down into stacked figures.
Caption/VO: "So when a place charges ₹90, something in this list got cut."
*Structure: Hook / Proof / Payoff — the breakdown earns the opening claim, then flips it into a reason the price makes sense.*

## CTA
**On-screen + final frame:** "Next time you see a cheap espresso — now you know what's missing."
**Ask (one, quote-post-shaped):** Pin a reply or end-card line: *"The ₹31 coffee is the part we'll never cut. Everything else is negotiable."*
